subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity API lands, or should core expose activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new core feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an existing contract.

options.title: Keep As Downstream Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 and design the watchdog only after the canonical activity contract is accepted.

options.title: Route Delivery Outside Core
options.body: Keep only activity and diagnostics in core while plugins, dashboards, or operator integrations own alert delivery and templates.

options.title: Defer The Watchdog
options.body: Leave the request parked until real operator usage shows which alert classes and privacy constraints are worth a core feature.

recommendation.title: Keep As Downstream Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 and design the watchdog only after the canonical activity contract is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the live prerequisite activity-contract issue and has recent gateway/protocol-adjacent history.
